notes.text: Mishnah Yoma commemorates and praises the donor. “Pious” is Heilprin’s characterization, not a literal epithet in that Mishnah.

Pesachim specifies the gap in sanctification for inserting thumbs. Leviticus 14:14 supplies the ritual referent: the priest puts sacrificial blood on the right thumb.
Mishnah Yoma records the miracles and public praise. Bavli elaborates on bringing the doors from Alexandria.
Tosefta Yoma narrates the threatened loss of the second door and locates the return of the first door at Jaffa.
The Bavli and Tosefta say he went to bring or brought the doors from Alexandria. The root separately says he made them. Preserve Heilprin’s account alongside the comparison.
Bavli describes his grasping or embracing the other door and volunteering to be thrown with it, after which the sea calms. Preserve Heilprin’s stronger tied-himself wording as the root’s report.
Bavli locates the return of the door at Acre and Tosefta at Jaffa. Heilprin does not name the port here, and both formulations remain separately documented.
The respective primary versions mention a sea creature that swallowed and expelled the door. The root’s great fish remains as its own formulation.
